⠀
Andrew Kolvet built deep ties to American Christian Zionism, major pro-Israel donors, and Israel’s diplomatic and PR apparatus in the United States.
⠀
THE KAIROS COMPANY
⠀
• Kolvet spent four years at The Kairos Company, the PR firm founded by Johnny Moore (former VP of Liberty University)
⠀
• Moore is a key intermediary between U.S. evangelical leaders and the Israeli government
⠀
• At Kairos, Kolvet ran campaigns that overlapped with pro-Israel advocacy
⠀
• The firm also represented PragerU and The Blaze
⠀
FRIENDS OF ZION AND THE ADELSONS
⠀
• In October 2017, Kolvet was listed as media contact for the Jerusalem Prayer Team
⠀
• The campaign, created by the Friends of Zion Heritage Center, claimed 20 million followers
⠀
• Tax filings (Form 990) showed the legal entity was registered as “Friends of the Aden Drug Clinic Inc.,” a Las Vegas methadone clinic
⠀
• Its directors were Sheldon and Miriam Adelson, among the most influential pro-Israel donors in the U.S.
⠀
TURNING POINT USA
⠀
• As TPUSA spokesman and executive producer of The Charlie Kirk Show, Kolvet oversaw the group’s pro-Israel programming
⠀
• TPUSA hosted pro-Israel speakers and fought BDS on campuses
⠀
• In January 2019, he handled PR for the first TPUSA Faith Pastors Tour of Israel, organized with Pastor Rob McCoy
⠀
• He also ran student focus groups. At a Tampa conference, 73% identified as pro-Israel
⠀
TRUMP, ADELSON, NETANYAHU
⠀
• According to Candace Owens, Kirk and Kolvet were present when Trump said, around July 2024, that Miriam Adelson offered $100 million for his campaign in exchange for accepting annexation of the West Bank
⠀
• Kolvet also confirmed that Netanyahu personally called Kirk with an offer of major funding to take TPUSA “to the next level”
⠀
• Kirk turned it down in the Hamptons
⠀
LEAKED CHATS AND THE FBI
⠀
• The MAGA split over Israel surfaced just before Kirk’s assassination in September 2025
⠀
• In October 2025, Owens leaked WhatsApp messages in which Kirk raged over losing a $2 million yearly donation from Robert Shillman
⠀
• Kirk said Jewish donors were “playing into all the stereotypes” and left him “no choice but to leave the pro-Israel cause”
⠀
• Kolvet confirmed the texts on air. He said he was “glad the truth is out,” because Kirk had struggled for months over speech limits on Israel’s policies
⠀
• He later said he submitted those messages to the FBI so any financial or geopolitical motive behind Kirk’s murder could be investigated

text:
A slowly warming world may be quietly nudging back the frozen boundaries of the North - the traditional margins of permafrost, arid tundra and the vast, mostly empty boreal forests.

However, studies now indicate that millions of square kilometres across Canada, Alaska, Scandinavia and Russia could cross critical thresholds for possible cultivation by the end of the century. 

Yet, transforming this vast northern frontier for farming or mining for minerals is not just a matter of waiting for the ice to melt—it would be a decades-long engineering and soil-transformation challenge.

The primary hurdle to a northern breadbasket is not temperature, but something called 'pedology' (the depleted chemistry of soils). Boreal and tundra soils are highly acidic, muddy and feature widespread peat bogs. They have very little deep root development, fungal growth or topsoil. 

Converting thawed land into tillable soil for grains like barley, rye, and oilseeds will need extensive soil conditioning and nutrient management. There would be no immediate crop harvests.

Ice-rich permafrost does not just melt into prairie with roaming buffalo, like the great plains of America. It would undergo 'thermokarst' degradation, collapsing into a mosaic of slumping ground, thermokarst lakes and wetland bogs. 

Heavy machinery cannot operate on such an unstable surface, meaning large-scale agriculture and master-planned settlements would have to concentrate in well-drained river valleys, ancient glacial outwash plains, and bedrock-stable corridors rather than open tundra.

The solar geometry of the far North has a unique biological dynamic. While 20-hour summer days offer unprecedented sunlight periods that drive plant growth cycles, the low angle of light means solar irradiance stays lower than traditional mid-latitude grain belts.

From an infrastructure perspective, opening the North would face severe logistical constraints. Thawing out muddy ground can shear road foundations, buckle rail lines and complicate building design. Realising the region's huge potential—such as access to critical minerals, rare earths and fresh water reserves—will need specific engineering techniques and heavy investment in road access.

Opening up the high latitudes echoes the great frontier eras of human history, but faces an engineering quagmire.

It could not happen overnight; but is more likely to be a series of centuries-long engineering challenges to liberate the far north. Human ingenuity, soil science, and structural engineering could only gradually reshape these wild, empty regions.
